newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at record high.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a strong week with their fifth consecutive record despite giving up most of their early gains towards the end of the session on profit taking and an easier Wall Street opening.
Dealers said stocks such CS Group, Roche and Novartis were also influenced by derivatives-linked transactions.
Looking ahead, one trader noted that the market would closely follow the U.S. Federal Reserve's meeting on May 20.
"The markets are split on whether the Fed will raise interest rates," he added.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index gained 15.8 points, or 0.31 percent, to end at 5,157.5 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index was up 9.94 points, or 0.31 percent, to 3,255.86.
Bourse volume stood at 2.79 billion francs.

UBS, which has been in the limelight among financials for the past few sessions, rose six francs to 1,499. Rival CS Group was heavily traded, ending up 0.25 francs at 172 after reaching a 1997 high of 176.75 francs.

Dealers said the brief but strong intra-day rise may have been due to market expectations that CS Group may soon complete the sale of the industrial activities of its Elektrowatt unit to Germany's Siemens.

Roche was up 295 francs, or 2.23 percent, to 13,495. The stock's rise was due partly to derivatives transactions and partly to earlier news that its weight loss drug Xenical was recommended for approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's advisory panel, share dealers said.
Novartis registered shares slid 17 francs to 2,011. ABB eased 19 to 1,971.
